# Northstar — Monday Business Review
**Prepared by: Product & Growth Lead | Basis: Sept–Oct 2026 data pack only**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

- **The revenue "growth" is a billing artifact.** October invoiced revenue (€873.4k) looks +9.6% vs September (€797.1k), but €120k of that is gringotts' 12-month annual prepay and €19.5k is a duplicate invoice. Normalized MRR is **€746.1k → €757.7k (+1.6%) — essentially flat.**
- **Churn is the real story.** 5 customers (€303.6k ARR) churned in October — 13.9% of logos, 3.4% of MRR in one month. Four were SMB-starter (44% of the starter base). SMB gross adds in October (€11.1k MRR) barely exceeded SMB churn (€10.3k MRR).
- **Enterprise is the fortress:** 77% of ARR, zero churn, zero contraction, €216k of expansion booked in October (billing from November), usage +8.3% ex-Acme. Acme's −45% request drop is the documented batch migration, not churn (tokens only −12%).
- **The paid-search headline is an attribution artifact.** Its €274.8k attributed revenue is 76% expansion credit on 2023–24 enterprise logos. On new logos, partner (€166.8k, 2 logos) and content (€91.2k, 3 logos) lead. Paid search's incremental October leads trialed at **3.7%** vs the 8.5% baseline.
- **Enterprise plan = 87% of revenue and 79% of gross profit, but margin fell 32.2% → 29.5% in one month** on support-cost growth. Pro is the margin leader (62.7%).
- **Bottom line on the three decisions:** (1) don't cut a segment wholesale — SMB has a retention problem, not proven value destruction; (2) don't raise paid search on this evidence; (3) point engineering at the enterprise plan's reliability and cost-to-serve. **CAC payback cannot be calculated from this pack — no channel spend data exists in it.**

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

**Invoiced revenue vs. real MRR** (revenue.csv records invoices at full value when dated; subscriptions are billed in advance):

| | Sept | Oct (deduped) |
|---|---|---|
| Subscriptions | €746.1k | €867.7k (incl. gringotts €120k annual) |
| Professional services (one-off) | €51.0k | €5.7k |
| **Invoiced total** | **€797.1k** | **€873.4k** |
| **MRR-normalized** (gringotts at €10k/mo) | **€746.1k** | **€757.7k (+1.6%)** |

- €25.3k of October's MRR belongs to customers who churned mid-month but were invoiced in advance on Oct 1 (nakatomi €15k, buy-n-large €3.3k, mega-lo-mart €2.7k, dinoco €2.3k, slate-rock €2k). **November starts at ~€750.4k** (757.7 − 25.3 + 18 expansion) before any new sales — a step-down that is *not* November's performance.
- **ARR bridge (Sept 1 → today):** €8,953k → €8,789k = **−€164k (−1.8%)**. Components: +€246k Sept logos, +€133k Oct logos, +€36k hooli expansion, −€30k soylent contraction (downgraded €264k → €234k), −€304k churn. A further **€216k of expansion booked in October bills from November** (stark +€84k, umbrella +€48k, globex +€42k, cyberdyne +€24k, massive-dynamic +€18k annualised).

**What's driving the headline numbers:**
- **Enterprise segment (77% of ARR, €6,780k):** zero churn, zero contraction, all large expansions, usage +8.3% ex-Acme (17.8M → 19.3M requests). Acme's −45% requests matches the documented batch migration (est. 40–50% interactive reduction); tokens fell only 12% and users 240→232. *Not a churn signal.* Watch item: Acme went from 140% of its 3M included requests to 84% — overage billing at its Feb 2027 renewal may shrink.
- **SMB (5.4% of ARR, €479k):** 4 of 12 September SMB logos churned in October (44% of the starter base). All four showed **−35% to −37% usage declines before churning** — a usable early-warning signal. SMB October gross adds (€11.1k MRR) barely exceeded SMB churn (€10.3k MRR).
- **Most at-risk account today: soylent** (mid-market, enterprise plan, €234k ARR): usage −27%, users 56→41, downgraded −11%, and 8 October tickets including the pack's only *critical*. Nakatomi (€180k) showed the same pattern before churning: usage decline + unresolved high-sev api_errors.
- **Support volume +25%** (59 → 74 tickets). Rate-limit tickets tripled (4 → 13), concentrated in pro customers exceeding their 600k included requests (wonka 1.02M, aperture 705k, vandelay 690k). Open high-sev at month-end: **stark** (api_errors), **contoso** (api_errors), **wayne** (performance), soylent.

---

## 3. ACQUISITION

**What can be concluded — new-logo performance only (Sept + Oct):**

| Channel | New logos | New-logo ARR | Avg logo | Lead→trial (2 mo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Partner | 2 | €166.8k | €83.4k | 23.7% (32/135) |
| Content | 3 | €91.2k | €30.4k | 11.0% (65/590) |
| Paid search | 2 | €64.8k | €32.4k | 7.2% (102/1,420) |
| Outbound | 2 | €56.4k | €28.2k | 5.9% (21/355) |

**What cannot be concluded:**
- **Paid search's headline (€274.8k attributed) is an attribution artifact.** €210k (76%) is expansion credit on stark, umbrella, globex, hooli — customers acquired in 2023–24. That is retention, not channel acquisition. On new logos, paid search is second-smallest.
- **The October paid-search surge diluted quality.** Leads +73% (520→900, new campaign started 28 Sep); trials +32%; the *incremental* 380 leads converted to trial at **14/380 = 3.7%** vs the 8.5% September baseline. Downstream value is unknowable — trial-to-paid is not tracked.
- **CAC and CAC payback by channel (CFO ask): not calculable.** The pack has zero spend data. The model is ready — *payback (months) = CAC ÷ (new-logo ARR × plan gross margin ÷ 12)* — but needs Sept/Oct spend by channel from finance/marketing.
- Partner looks best on quality but runs at only 60–75 leads/month; scalability is unproven. Content is the only channel producing both new logos and an expansion (massive-dynamic).

---

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS (October, plans.csv)

| Plan | MRR | Infra | Support | Gross profit | Margin | Sept margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | €659.5k | €296.8k | €168.0k | €194.7k | **29.5%** | 32.2% |
| Pro | €66.2k | €16.1k | €8.6k | €41.5k | **62.7%** | 67.5% |
| Starter | €32.0k | €11.4k | €10.3k | €10.3k | 32.2% | 34.9% |
| **Blended** | €757.7k | | | €246.5k | **32.5%** | **35.2%** |

- **Enterprise plan:** 87% of revenue, 79% of gross profit — but margin fell 2.7pp in a month. Costs grew +€17.8k (+4.0%) against revenue +€0.5k. Support is **€12.0k/customer/month (25.5% of plan revenue)**, driven by high-sev api_errors/performance load — soylent alone went 3 → 8 tickets. Infra per token is stable (~€11.7/M tokens); support is the growing cost.
- **Pro:** best margin and the clearest monetization path — 3 of 9 pro customers exceeded their 600k included requests in October; overage bills at renewal (wayne's enterprise-plan overage renews **30 Nov**; wonka +70% over included renews March 2027). 13 rate-limit tickets = friction today, pricing power tomorrow.
- **Starter:** margin-positive but thin; ex-churn starter MRR *shrank* (€24.1k → €21.7k) despite 4 new logos. A revolving door, not an engine.
- Caveat: **plan ≠ segment** — the enterprise plan includes 6 mid-market accounts; pro mixes mid-market and SMB.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **Segment investment (Finance): Do not approve a wholesale cut this week.** The case against SMB is retention (44% of starter logos churned in October; churn eats ~all SMB gross adds), but SMB is gross-margin positive (32%+), supplies **8 of 9 new logos**, and contains the fastest-ramping accounts (planet-express +49%, monsters +53%). Instead: **freeze incremental SMB acquisition spend**, run a 60-day retention sprint built on the proven trigger (usage down >30% → intervention), and set a January checkpoint — cut only if SMB net revenue retention hasn't improved. There is no case for cutting Enterprise or Mid-market.
2. **Acquisition channel (Growth): Do not increase paid search on today's evidence** — its headline is expansion attribution, and incremental October leads trialed at 3.7% vs the 8.5% baseline. Hold all channel spend flat; re-report channels on **new-logo ARR only**; deliver CAC payback within a week of receiving channel spend data. If leadership wants action now, run a **time-boxed partner pilot with a hard cost cap** (best trial rate and logo value, unproven scale).
3. **Plan focus (Product): Enterprise plan — reliability and cost-to-serve.** It carries 79% of gross profit; margin is eroding ~3pp/month; high-sev api_errors/performance tickets remain open at the three largest accounts; and one enterprise churn (stark = €1.14M) would erase more ARR than a full quarter of new logos. Concretely: an API error-rate/performance program plus first-class batch-workload support (Acme's migration is the template). **Secondary:** pro-plan rate-limit/overage experience — it converts existing friction into renewal revenue. Deprioritize starter engineering.
4. **Protect November's number:** assign named coverage to soylent and the open high-sev tickets at stark, contoso, and wayne; confirm the €216k expansion lands in November invoices as expected.

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

1. **Duplicate invoice:** INV-2026-10-0209 (soylent, €19,500) appears twice — stripe 1 Oct and billing_sync 2 Oct. Naive October revenue is overstated by €19.5k (€892.9k vs €873.4k). Dedupe on transaction_id; audit the billing_sync pipeline (its only record is the duplicate).
2. **Invoiced ≠ earned:** advance billing (gringotts €120k) and mid-month churn after advance invoicing (€25.3k) distort MoM comparisons. October's invoices (issued 1–3 Oct) largely cover November. Use plans.csv MRR for trend.
3. **CAC / CAC payback / channel ROI: not calculable** — no spend data in the pack. Also, funnel.csv "conversions" are **paid-trial starts**, not customers; trial-to-paid runs on a longer cycle and is untracked. Any "lead conversion rate" computed from funnel.csv is the wrong stage.
4. **Attribution inflation:** €252k of €631.2k credited revenue (40%) is expansion bookings credited to channels for 2023–24 logos; €210k of paid search's €274.8k is of this type. Expansion bookings also take effect the *following* cycle — October credit ≠ October performance.
5. **Segment P&L cannot be built:** costs are attributed by plan, and plans cut across segments. Finance's segment question currently rests on churn and usage signals, not segment profitability.
6. **ARR field semantics:** churned rows retain arr_eur (€303.6k total) — naive totals overstate current ARR. Soylent's arr_eur already reflects its downgrade (consistent with its €19.5k invoice) — confirm intended behavior.
7. **Small, lumpy sample:** two months, 36 customers; nakatomi alone is 59% of churned ARR. Naive annualization of October churn (~34% ARR) overstates steady state — though SMB-starter churn (~43% of starter MRR in one month) is unambiguously severe.
8. **Usage pipeline anomaly:** customers churning mid-October show near-full-month usage (slate-rock churned 8 Oct yet −34.7%, not ~−75%) — verify how the usage pipeline treats partial months. `usage_change_pct` is blank for new accounts (expected, no base month).
9. **Two months only:** no seasonality baseline; October cohort outcomes not yet observable; PS revenue (€51k Sept / €5.7k Oct) is one-off and excluded from MRR throughout.
